question: What two movements arise when the supreme meets its own sameness?
premises: When the supreme relates to its own sameness, a twofold movement arises.
One of these is simply the supreme itself.
That one can serve for the production of bliss.
inference: Therefore the supreme's self-relation yields two movements, one of which generates bliss.
uncertainties: The verse breaks mid-thought and continues into 161; the inference is limited to what is explicit here.
plain_english: When the supreme meets its own sameness, a twofold movement arises. One of these remains simply the supreme and can give rise to bliss.
